text: To break the silence, Gabriel mentioned, in a false voice, that Freddy Malins had paid back the money he owed him, and he added that Freddy was a decent fellow after all. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly Gretta came to him, stood on tiptoe to kiss him, and said softly that he was a very generous person, and for a moment his heart trembled with a happiness he had not expected. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet when he held her close and asked what she was thinking about, she was silent at first, and only after he pressed her again did she answer that she was thinking of that song. <break time="0.8s" /> It was The Lass of Aughrim, the very song she had heard on the stairs, and as she spoke its name she broke away from him, threw herself upon the bed, and hid her face. <break time="0.8s" /> Gabriel stood still for a moment in astonishment, and then, passing the mirror on his way to her, he caught sight of himself, a man whose face always puzzled him in a glass. <break time="0.8s" /> Standing near her, he asked why the song made her cry, and between her sobs she told him that she was thinking of a person who used to sing it long ago in Galway. <break time="0.8s" /> His name was Michael Furey, she said, a delicate boy whom she had known when she was a girl living with her grandmother, and she used to go out walking with him. <break time="0.8s" /> Gabriel, a cold irony in his voice, suggested that perhaps she wanted to go to Galway to see him, but she looked away in silence and at length answered that the boy had died at only seventeen.
